instruction: Use Abaqus through the graphical user interface to perform a tensile analysis of a rectangular solid block. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (12, 8) in the Y-Z plane and extrude along the global X-axis to a length of 120 mm. This produces a block with cross-section 12 mm x 8 mm and overall length 120 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Aluminum with Young's modulus E = 70000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.33. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Aluminum and assign it to the entire block. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the block. Analysis Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Load. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply an Encastre boundary condition to the end face at X = 0. Apply a uniform pressure of 8.33 MPa to the end face at X = 120 mm, acting in the global positive X direction. This pressure is equivalent to a total tensile force of 800 N over the 12 mm x 8 mm cross-section. Discretization: Mesh the block with a global seed size of 4 mm. Assign the element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-BlockTension, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Post-Processing: Open the output database. Review the S11 stress contour at the mid-section (X approximately 60 mm). Query the U1 displacement at the node located at the center of the free end face (X = 120 mm, Y = 6 mm, Z = 4 mm). Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-BlockTension.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-BlockTension.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated. You must complete all operations interactively through the abaqus graphical user interface (GUI) step by step. The use of external script files is strictly prohibited.
